body: **2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** — added the confirm windows to §8 Timeout extensions: a confirmed `viola send` waits up to `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI up to its own 40 s window. If not confirmed in time it fails `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`, and the bound falls on the driver only. This is the closest precedent for this chunk: a post-condition ledger row for a local command. Any `/context` confirm window joins the bounds that rows contract/send-refusal/no-prompt-submitted, decision/time-bounds-never-on-human and decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver list, so a new or reused window must be said to fall on the driver and never on a key.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — a verified send waits in the readiness gate (at most 8.5 s), then is refused `input-not-ready` with nothing typed. A human key during that wait takes the wheel, and the send is refused `human-typing`. The case `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins` is sequenced on records, never on a timer. The `/context` paste goes through this same gate (rows contract/send-refusal/input-not-ready, decision/human-key-takes-the-wheel, decision/boundary-tests-sequenced-on-records), so the human must still win during any `/context` send.

It is PROVISIONAL (delegate overseer). This is the latest precedent for a new ledger row with a `viola verify` probe. The `/context` probe adds a step line, and the absent word must stay scoped to that one row unless the plan amends it.

The stop path adds no time bound. A new interactive verify probe (the `/context` paste) must keep this behaviour on Ctrl-C or TERM (rows contract/interrupted-verify/exit, contract/interrupted-verify/stderr, contract/viola-verify/interrupted-pair).

Carry cry-kutofxml is folded into this chunk: the next reading of the placeholder hint covers every drawn cell past the cursor, attributes only. That reading has to stay inside this exception or amend it.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — ~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver and ~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human dropped the budget pause. ~ contract/cli-exit-codes/11 retired exit 11, never to be reused. The per-behaviour CLI capability ledger as the single gate for CLI behaviour: the new row is version-stamped, and a behaviour is relied on only through a stamped row.

Whether the new row is relied: a CLI version reads verified only when every relied row counts, so a relied row makes every stamped version read unverified until re-stamped; and no probe is written for a shape no send relies on.

The local-command echo ledger row and its verify probe: a compiled-literal paste in an interactive verify run, verify waiting for its input-box literal after added turns, screen signatures as compiled literals.

The verify run's limits the new probe must keep: verify is the sole stamps writer, a stamps merge replaces only its own version, verify never types into a CLI dialog, verify's bounded child set and its own probe folders removed by drop guard.
The ledger stamps envelope: the rows the new stamp adds, the verified version, and its single writer under a strict-modes check before and under its lock.

Every send confirmed after the fact: a send whose post-condition is not measured on the CLI version answers ok with confirmed false and detail unconfirmable; unconfirmed delivery never reads as delivered.
The send results and the send-confirmed event: the send-issued, send-confirmed and send-refused records the wrapper appends and their order in the events log, for a /context send.
The compiled confirmation window and the send time bound inside which the /context post-condition is read.

Recorded fixtures only from a clean verify, scrubbed and hygiene-walked, screen fixtures keeping only signature rows, should the probe record one.
